sections.title: PhD Dissertation (defended 4 September 2026)
content: "Painful temporomandibular disorders and headache in young adulthood: early-life factors and multidimensional clinical characterization," Aarhus University.

The dissertation examined whether early-life factors — adolescent dietary quality and prenatal nutrition — are associated with painful temporomandibular disorders (TMD) and headache in young adulthood, and characterized the pain, psychosocial, somatosensory, and lifestyle profile of young adults with painful TMD, using data from the Danish National Birth Cohort.

sections.title: Current Postdoctoral Research: Life-Course and Epigenetic Analyses of Painful Temporomandibular Disorders
content: This postdoctoral project is a direct continuation of Mojdeh's PhD work. Its overall aim is to investigate epigenetic mechanisms underlying vulnerability to p-TMD, building on the epidemiological and clinical findings from her PhD within the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC).

The project uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling (Illumina EPIC arrays) on biological samples and clinical phenotyping data collected during the PhD, to identify epigenetic markers associated with p-TMD and examine whether fetal exposure, childhood diet, and adolescent lifestyle factors relate to differential DNA methylation patterns.
It is carried out in collaboration with Professor Lene Baad-Hansen (Aarhus University), Associate Professor Bodil Hammer Bech (Aarhus University), and Professor Luda Diatchenko (McGill University).
